text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak to meet U.S. Middle East envoy today Dennis Ross. Talks will cover U.S. moves to save peace.

- The International Monetary Fund confirms the Egyptian economy will make a strong take off in the coming years. Inflation rate is expected to decline in 1998 to 5.5 percent, the IMF representative in Cairo said.
- Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi says that the ministry plans to increase the porduction of natural gas and derivatives in the next three years to 2.5 billion cubit feet per day from 1.6 billion now.
- Mubarak to leave for Morocco within days to hold talks with King Hassan II on the issue of Jerusalem and bilateral relations.

- Mubarak to visit Germany on May 20. Mubarak's talks with German leaders during his one-day visit will deal with the European role in the peace process and obsatcles on the way to signing an association agreement between Egypt and the European Union.
- The Central Bank Governor Ismail Hassan says that the budget deficit will decline, for the firt time, to less than one percent of GDP.

- Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati says that Egypt is an important member of the Organisation of Islmaic Conference and the Non-Alignment Movement and will play an important role at the next Islamic summit in Iran.
